_comment: Tracks progress through a single Monday weekly-batch cycle (21 shorts + 7 long-form). Written/read by whichever session is running the batch so an interrupted run (session limit, crash, etc.) can resume from the last incomplete item instead of restarting from scratch or double-producing already-published items. Reset to a fresh empty 'current_batch' at the start of each new Monday firing, but keep prior batches in 'history' for audit.

current_batch.week_range_note: First real batch run fired mid-Monday-evening (20:43 UTC) as a manual test of the trigger — all of Monday 2026-07-27's own slots had already passed by the time this ran, so the entire 7-day/28-item schedule was shifted to start Tuesday 2026-07-28 through Monday 2026-08-03 instead, to avoid scheduling any publishAt in the past (YouTube rejects that outright). Future automatic Monday-06:00-UTC firings won't have this problem since they start at the beginning of the day.
current_batch.upload_quota_blocker_note: 2026-07-27T23:55Z: YouTube returned uploadLimitExceeded on sf_019's publish attempt (and would affect any subsequent publish this same period — this is a per-channel daily cap, not per-video). 9 shorts and 2 long-form videos were already successfully published/scheduled today before this hit (sf_012-sf_018 published earlier in the session, sf_013-018+lf_002 reupload+lf_003 in this batch run = roughly 11 uploads today total). sf_019/sf_020/sf_021 are fully produced and gate-passed but blocked on this quota — see their publish_blocker notes in state/short_form_queue.json. Do not keep retrying the same upload in a tight loop; wait for the quota window to reset (next UTC day is the safest assumption) before attempting more publishes. Continuing to SCOUT/SCRIPT/PRODUCE further items is still fine and useful (keeps work ready to publish immediately once quota resets) but PUBLISHING is paused.
current_batch.publishing_model_note: 2026-07-27T21:35Z: Restructured to a two-phase model after hitting YouTube's daily upload quota (uploaded ~11 videos within about an hour of wall-clock time, even though publishAt spread them across the week). PRODUCTION (script/produce/gate) has no per-day cap -> items land at 'ready_to_publish'. PUBLISHING is capped to ~4 uploads (3 shorts + 1 long-form) per real 24h period, matching the daily trigger's new cadence. sf_019/sf_020/sf_021 were fully produced/gated today but hadn't actually reached their scheduled day yet (2026-07-30) when the quota hit -- moved to 'ready_to_publish' to reflect that they were never actually supposed to upload today under the corrected model, not just quota-blocked.
current_batch.upload_quota_reset_timing_note: 2026-07-28T06:10Z: retried lf_004's publish (blocked since ~2026-07-27T23:55Z). Still uploadLimitExceeded ~9-10h later. Confirms the quota reset window is longer than 9-10h and does NOT simply flip at UTC midnight or a fixed 'next calendar day' boundary. Will keep retrying on future firings without looping within a single firing; once a retry succeeds, note the actual elapsed time here so this pipeline learns the real window empirically instead of guessing.
current_batch.clip_pool_provenance_note: 2026-07-28T06:45Z: while spot-checking clip content for sf_022-024, discovered that the entire original raw clip pool (assets/short-form-clips/raw/1.mp4-60.mp4, used in every short published so far, sf_002 through sf_021) is sourced from a 'Download link in description' split-screen repost/scrape-compilation format — every source file is 1920x1080 landscape with a white sidebar and that text baked in. This was not previously caught because scripts/short_form_transform.py's center crop (crop='min(iw,ih*9/16)':'min(ih,iw*16/9)') happens to land almost exactly on the visible video content and excludes the white sidebars entirely — verified by cropping a sample frame: the watermark is fully removed in every published output, confirmed nothing has ever gone out visibly watermarked. This does NOT change technical viability of the existing pipeline, but it does mean the source footage itself is repost/scrape-provenance content (same category of copyright risk as the already-accepted 'unmitigated third-party clip reuse' risk in config/gates.json copyright_gate, just now known to apply to the whole 60-clip pool rather than assumed to be cleaner raw footage). The second-batch clips (61.mp4-70.mp4, Drive folder 19ZYbWZlya3_s_W4TpTbXHs1unUHW2wp7) are genuinely clean — already-vertical 720x1280, no watermark, no sidebar. Flagged to the channel owner directly; no change made to the existing accepted-risk framework since it's a discovery within an already-accepted risk category, not a new one.
